objective: Hide one coarse receiver-retirement operation behind source execution, without chunked snapshots or additional threads; measure both downtime and the work moved outside it
sub_1ms_interpretation: One isolated sub-1ms sample in the proactive RCU1 control does not establish a sub-1ms median or sustained guarantee; primary and all matched-case medians remain above 1ms.

definitions.prepare: One PrepareReuse HTTP action and one vCPU-channel event per incoming handoff. Local invariant validation, old PIT stop, strict IRQFD deassign/flush, eventfd drain, EFER.NX invalidation. No guest-memory writes or KVM_RUN.
definitions.save_restore: Per-round source snapshot API + destination load API, then percentile. Preparation is excluded and separately measured.
definitions.save_restore_prepare: Per-round elapsed time of all three APIs. Includes waits and thread wakeup; this is not CPU time and not wall-clock downtime because prepare overlaps execution.
definitions.handoff: Source Pause request begin to remote guest ACK observed by source.
definitions.destination_ready_wait: Controller wait for destination ready, after dwell in prepared mode; before dwell in unchanged legacy mode.
definitions.request_to_ack: Prepared mode: contiguous time from after dwell/before ready wait through ACK. Legacy mode: from Pause request through ACK; use scheduling_wait_plus_handoff to include legacy ready wait.
definitions.scheduling_wait_plus_handoff: Ready wait duration + Pause-to-ACK duration. Includes readiness cost in all modes; excludes the deliberate dwell interval.
definitions.cycle: Source-loop entry to ACK, including ready wait, heap-verification wait and deliberate dwell. Excludes previous destination post-ACK diagnostics; not a global inter-ACK throughput interval.
definitions.profiling: Separate profiled runs; nested child scopes cannot be added to parent scopes. The conditional translation stage also includes identity logging, so a prepared value is not zero despite skipping NX ioctl.
definitions.no_lead_control: --reuse-prepare-on-demand makes the retiring worker wait for the next source request generation before starting the same PrepareReuse action. Request-to-ACK therefore includes actual preparation readiness delay despite post-ACK heap-validation slack. Initial seed preparation remains outside measurements.

implementation.state_machine: Paused -> Prepared -> restored Paused -> Running. Duplicate prepare is idempotent. Validation failure leaves Prepared retryable; native partial failure poisons worker.
implementation.ordering: Seed B prepares after Pause. Retiring source snapshots, publishes, observes peer ACK, then prepares its local worker and publishes ready for the next incoming generation. Next source runs dwell before waiting for ready.
implementation.retained: Native KVM VM/vCPU/VMCS allocation, FDs, thread and fixed DAX mapping; zero new VM/vCPU/thread creation during restore.
implementation.scope: No new production executable, kernel source change or QEMU source change.

limitations: No record-wise serialization pipeline; the existing whole-state codec and CPU setter ordering remain.
No claim that preparation removes its work; API sum and readiness/cycle metrics retain it.
When little execution time is available, preparation can delay the requested handoff while the source stays running.

Zero deliberate dwell is not zero preparation lead time: post-ACK retained-heap checks/diagnostics still allow preparation to overlap. Separate on-demand controls force preparation to start after the request.
Cooperative single-owner protocol; no distributed fencing/crash recovery.
Same DAX allocation only; general I/O, differing configurations and physical multi-host CXL performance remain unverified.
Default production seccomp rules do not cover the added runtime ioctl paths; experiments use --no-seccomp.
